images.title: Two copies of one group
images.purpose: Show that 4 cakes for 10 children is two copies of 2 cakes for 5 children, so every child gets the same share: 2/5 = 4/10.
images.composition: Two identical boxed groups side by side with a wide gap, and one result line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left box, outlined teal #0072B2: 2 round cakes of the same size, each cut into 5 equal slices, plain fill. Right box, outlined amber #E69F00: exactly the same, 2 round cakes of the same size, each cut into 5 equal slices. Each box has its caption under it. A thin grey #6B7280 bracket spans both boxes from below, with the result line under it. No children drawn. Exactly 2 boxes, 4 cakes, 20 slices.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered

images.takeaway: Two copies of the same sharing give the same share, so 2/5 = 4/10.
images.description: Two identical groups of 2 cakes, each cake cut into 5 equal slices, one for 5 children and one for 5 more; together 4 cakes for 10 children, and 2/5 = 4/10.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say why the right box is an exact copy of the left box, and so each child's share does not change.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the bigger sharing as two copies of the smaller one is a picture idea; one image carries it.
